title: Four-Team Single-Elimination Bracket
description:
Simulate a 4-team single-elimination tournament. The winner of a match is the team with the **higher skill**. Round 1 pairings are in `matches`. The final is winner of match 1 vs winner of match 2.

**Tables:** `teams` (`team_id`, `name`, `skill`), `matches` (`round`, `match_id`, `team_a`, `team_b`)

Output columns: `round`, `match_id`, `winner`, `loser`. Order by `round`, `match_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE teams (team_id INT, name VARCHAR, skill INT); INSERT INTO teams VALUES (1,'Alpha',90),(2,'Bravo',70),(3,'Charlie',80),(4,'Delta',60); CREATE TABLE matches (round INT, match_id INT, team_a INT, team_b INT); INSERT INTO matches VALUES (1,1,1,4),(1,2,2,3);
solution_sql: WITH r1 AS (SELECT m.round, m.match_id, CASE WHEN ta.skill >= tb.skill THEN ta.name ELSE tb.name END AS winner, CASE WHEN ta.skill >= tb.skill THEN tb.name ELSE ta.name END AS loser FROM matches m JOIN teams ta ON ta.team_id = m.team_a JOIN teams tb ON tb.team_id = m.team_b), r2 AS (SELECT 2 AS round, 3 AS match_id, CASE WHEN t1.skill >= t2.skill THEN t1.name ELSE t2.name END AS winner, CASE WHEN t1.skill >= t2.skill THEN t2.name ELSE t1.name END AS loser FROM r1 w1 JOIN teams t1 ON t1.name = w1.winner AND w1.match_id = 1 JOIN r1 w2 ON w2.match_id = 2 JOIN teams t2 ON t2.name = w2.winner) SELECT round, match_id, winner, loser FROM r1 UNION ALL SELECT round, match_id, winner, loser FROM r2 ORDER BY round, match_id

test_cases.description: Alpha beats Delta, Charlie beats Bravo, Alpha wins the final

hints: Join matches to teams twice (team_a and team_b) and CASE on skill to pick winner/loser.
The final CTE joins the two round-1 winners back to teams and compares skill again.
explanation: Match 1: Alpha 90 > Delta 60. Match 2: Charlie 80 > Bravo 70. Final: Alpha 90 > Charlie 80. Two CTEs plus UNION ALL produce the full bracket without needing a recursive walk for only two rounds.
